html:
Polotsk is the oldest town of Belarus, on the Western Dvina River in the north, first named in the chronicles under the year 862 and seat of the medieval Principality of Polotsk.

Its princes, descended from Vladimir the Great and the Polotsk princess Rogneda, often went their own way from Kyiv. Polotsk traded down the Dvina to the Baltic and built its own Saint Sophia Cathedral in the 1000s. Saint Euphrosyne of Polotsk founded a convent there in the 1100s. Weakened by German crusaders and Lithuanian raids, it passed into the Grand Duchy of Lithuania by the early 1300s. Belarusians count Polotsk as the cradle of their statehood.
sum: Polotsk is the oldest town of Belarus, on the Western Dvina River in the north, first named in the chronicles under the year 862 and seat of the medieval Principality of Polotsk.
